title: Introduce cost-handyman: defaults assembler and quant profiles serializer
author: Priya Rao
description:
Motivation: Tenants frequently override batching/caching defaults and shipping quantization profiles is brittle. This PR introduces 'cost-handyman' — a small orchestration binary and library that assembles tenant-facing defaults (batch shapes, cache window, prefill thresholds) and exports deterministic, versioned quantization profile bundles (JSON + proto) for downstream runtime and Dedicated/Private installers.

Summary: Adds an assembler service that: 1) merges global defaults, tenant overrides and workload-sampled signals into a canonical defaults manifest; 2) serializes quant profiles and a light checksum for safe rollouts; 3) emits telemetry hooks so Optimize/Console can surface suggested deltas; 4) provides a CLI dry-run and a declarative import endpoint for admin workflows.

What's included (high-level): assembled defaults algorithm with conservative fallthroughs, quant profile serializer (v1 JSON + protobuf schema), CLI (dry-run, push, rollback), SDK helpers for Python/Go to consume assembled manifests, unit economics validator that flags >10% unit-cost regressions vs baseline.

Migration notes: Runtime will continue to accept legacy presets but will prefer a manifest annotated with manifest_version:1 produced by cost-handyman. During rollout we will enable the manifest consumer behind 'cost_defaults_v2' feature flag. There is a small data-migration job that converts existing tenant overrides to the new manifest shape (included as a one-shot script).

Checklist:
- [x] Core assembler library + tests
- [x] Quant serializer + proto + roundtrip tests
- [x] CLI: dry-run/push/rollback
- [x] Python SDK helpers and docs snippet
- [x] Telemetry hooks + sample dashboard queries
- [x] E2E smoke in staging

CI notes: Integration tests initially failed on the quant roundtrip due to proto mismatch; fixed by tightening the proto schema and bumping the compatibility tests. All CI checks passing on merge.

Risks: Low. Default merge behavior is conservative: the assembler never reduces tenant cache or batch windows by more than a configured percentage without explicit approval. The unit-econ validator blocks automatic pushes that would increase unit cost by >10%.

- Introduce cost-handyman: assembler service that composes batching/caching defaults
- Add deterministic quant profile serializer (JSON + protobuf) for safe rollouts
- CLI for dry-run/push/rollback and Python SDK helpers
- Unit-econ validator to guard against >10% unit-cost regressions
